# Cross-season patterns (from the hindsight notes)

Every item cites the season file it comes from. These are patterns in the author's notes, not general FRC claims.

## Guiding principles (author's catch phrases)
- **Build with your own means.** The offseason is the time to grow capabilities; in season, do what you already know.
  It is better to excel with a limited scope/complexity than to be mediocre at everything by trying to do too much.
- **Touch it, own it.** The intake must acquire a game piece the moment it touches it; the driver should not worry,
  just drive and trust the intake.
- **Steal from the best, invest the rest.** Use reference designs; don't reinvent the wheel when you don't need to.
- **We always use swerve.** Pre-2022 swerve was not the meta, but any redo of an old game assumes swerve.

## Simple, focused robots reach the top
- 2910 2018: 2-stage elevator, no wrist, climbed with the elevator – still one of the best ([2018](2018_power_up.md)).
- 2910 2019: low levels only – top game pieces per match; 973 2019 dropped the top rocket level and still ranked first
  in its division ([2019](2019_deep_space.md)).
- 973 2020: no under-spinner, no inner port, just fast cycles ([2020–21](2020_2021_infinite_recharge.md)).
- 695 2023 tilted fixed elevator + gripper; 1561 2023 cube-only launcher ([2023](2023_charged_up.md)).
- 2056/6329/3467 and 9496 2024 ([2024](2024_crescendo.md)); 1986 2013 dustpan for AUTO only
  ([2013](2013_ultimate_ascent.md)); 148/1011 2017 gear-only robot ([2017](2017_steamworks.md)).
- Complex robots also won when executed very well (971 2023, 1323 2025) – complexity is a cost, not a disqualifier.

## Light, low CoG, zippy
- 2910 2018/2019, 971 2019, 1690 2024 (high acceleration), 148 2017 (gear-only, geared for acceleration), 1561 2023.
- Small footprints to avoid defense: 2910 2019, 971 2019, 4414 / 2910 2020.

## Intakes
- Mass acquisition wins for bulk pieces: 254 2017 ground intake ("touch it, own it"); 2026 wide ground intakes.
- Don't be picky: 2022 elite robots intaked any color and ejected opponent balls with a color sensor ("pooper").
- Orientation-sensitive pieces: floor intake of "any orientation" cones failed in 2023; successful robots restricted the
  orientation or the source (human player). 2025: star-wheel / wide-roller CORAL intakes with an inner straightening
  or centering stage before the handoff.
- Under-the-bumper intakes when AUTO centre-line collisions are likely (2024); over-the-bumper wide intakes were
  still used by a few very good robots (9483, 1778).
- Intakes that double as a scorer: 1323 / 694 / 422 2025 (place on L1), 9483 2024 (AMP), 5460 2023 (eject cubes).
- Recurring intake parts: top/bottom kicker rollers, polycord or belt centering (1577 2022, 1778 2025), mecanum
  centering (1690 2022, 2910/1114 2019), flap-down pivot (1323/4414 2022, 2023), linear rack-and-pinion
  deployment (254 2023).

## Bulk-piece capacity, indexing and rate
- Capacity matters for bulk pieces: 2017 (at least 50, elite about 100); 2026 elite about 50 (short expandable turret)
  and 60 (dumper), with outliers 85–110 (1114, 2481, 4414 – not representative).
- Collapsible hopper tops to pass under low field elements (2026): passive nets (most robots), 1678 active telescopic
  roof, 9128 thin flexible polycarbonate walls, 103 brushes.
- Indexing: active roller floors (254 2017, 2910/254 2026), spindexers (973 2017, 1690 2020), dye rotors (125/971
  2017, 1323/4414 2026), belt/polycord funneling (118 2017, 2910 2020).
- Two-lane shooters (254/973 2017) evolved into wide, divider-less multi-ball shooters (2026).

## Shooters
- Hood + small top wheels geared off the main flywheel to control spin: 2020 meta, reused in 2022 and 2026.
- Turret vs fixed: both reached the top in 2016, 2017, 2022 and 2026. Turrets were better under defense (2026);
  fixed/stop-and-shoot robots won on fast stop-to-shoot timing (2022) or a much higher rate (2026 dumpers).
- Catapults: 2014 (1678/33, motorized 469/1577) and 2016 (148/118/1986/195).
- Spin control for flat or oblong pieces: differential side wheels (2056/1678 2024).

## Placement structures and end effectors
- Elevator + wheeled gripper on a wrist: 2011 (254/1114), 2018 (254 and followers), 2019, 2025.
- Tilted fixed elevator: 695/4414/5940 2023, 1678/111/125/1706/5460 2024.
- Sideways elevator (first seen 3538 2018): 5460 2019, 971/1577 2019, 1690/4414/5940/1678 2025 – lets an arm swing
  180° without hitting the elevator.
- Utility arm / telescope on a low pivot: 1114 2014, 2910 2023 and 2025, 1323 2025, 67 2012, 2910 2019.
- Double-jointed arm (971 2018 lineage): 2056/5460 2023, 2630 2025.
- Gentle placement by opening a claw (254 2011, 2018); self-retracting / compliant end effectors that survive wall hits
  (254 2023, 3005 2025); mechanical alignment on the target (254/3005 2025, 1574 2017).
- Very light end effectors: vacuum (971 2019, 1690 2025), two compliant wheel rollers (1577/5460 2023).

## Human player as a design lever
- HP loading was the meta in 2013 (118 active HP intake); huge HP slides in 2025 (422 and others).
- Elite HPs placed pieces where robots want them: 2016 floor passes into the alliance zone, 2023 standing cones and
  throws to the loading-area edge, 2025 CORAL introduced near the REEF.
- HP timing as strategy: 2017 late gear staging hid the score.

## Endgame: only when it beats scoring
- No climbing in 2026; climb helpful but not critical in 2016; the 2024 TRAP "was a trap"; 2022 elite shooters could do
  a simpler climb and keep shooting.
- When climbs are decisive: everyone climbed in 2017, double/triple climbs in 2018 and 2019 (passive forklifts, ramps,
  rope hook-and-release), DEEP CAGE for almost all top robots in 2025.
- Simple, passive or single-actuator climbs recur: 2630 2013 wedge, velcro winch 2017, 254 servo-latched forklift 2018.

## AUTO and early control
- Early control decided games: 2018 scale (254's 4-cube AUTO), 2015 can stealing, 2014 3-ball AUTO, 2019 2–3 hatches.
- Reach tricks for AUTO only: 2910 2023 long floor extension, 1986 2013 dustpan, 2016 pre-dropped ball at a known spot.

## Strategy and alliance play
- Alliance role splits: 2014 three roles; 2016 two scorers + flex; 2018 two scale robots + flex; 2019 two do-it-all
  robots switching sides + defender; 2024 passers + clean-up, yet the champion was two cyclists + a defender.
- Disruption: 2022 shooting opponent balls into the far HANGAR; 2024 stealing passes; 1114 2014 AUTO blocker pole.
- Help partners: 2018 elite teams wrote their partners' AUTO before quals matches.
- Loopholes that "broke the game": 71 2002, 469 2010 ([2011 and earlier](2011_and_earlier.md)).
